title: The rows: target forms on an indefinite U(r), the volume of the chain of lifts as a product of lift volumes, and the height of each lift volume
summary: The rows are the good forms on the indefinite space Y₀ (target forms on U(r)). The volume 𝔷(ϑ) = det(Θ*Θ) of the chain Θ_ϑ of the m theta lifts restricted to the rows equals |c(ϑ)|^{rowDim} times the product of the volumes λ_j(ϑ^j) of the single lifts, with |c(θ(ι))/c(1)|^{−2} of controlled height (Data.volume_iota_eq_prod_liftVolume); and for a fit family of twists each ratio λ_j(1)/λ_j(θ(ι)^j) has height at most rowDim·k·(B₀·log b − 𝖴) (Data.heightLe_liftVolume_ratio): the rows repay the cost of the idle directions. The second bound rests on integral comparison forms built from auxiliary dual pairs, glued lattices and the carrier (an explicit theta lift of 1), whose descents see the twist only through one number made of Hecke L-values (exists_comparison_forms), and on height bounds for those Hecke value ratios.
chunk_title: Chunk 143-a: auxiliary dual pairs and stacked determinants, explicit matching and the carrier, crude jet bounds and point forms, glued lattices and product forms, vanishing theta periods, the volume of the chain, and the comparison forms
chunk_summary: Twelve modules of New/Rows (PartnerCut, SemiInvariantNorm, StackedDeterminants, RealMatching, Carrier, MemberKernels, GluedFormTheta, MonomialCoefficientVector, MemberOrthogonality, CartanIntegrality, RowVolume, ComparisonForms): the record of an auxiliary dual pair and its theta descent; the archimedean and global explicit matching of determinant polynomials and the carrier identity; crude integrality and conjugate bounds for theta jets; divided splittings, glued lattices and the theta lift of product forms; vanishing of theta periods for non-lifts; the factorisation of the chain volume; and the comparison forms with their integrality, size and adjoint identities.

members.name: FixesColsOff
members.statement_lean: abbrev FixesColsOff z
members.text: For a commutative ring R, finite types r and N, an embedding e : r ↪ N and an N×N matrix z over R, FixesColsOff e z is the proposition z·(1 − I_e·I_eᵀ) = 1 − I_e·I_eᵀ, where I_e = inclMatrix R e is the N×r matrix whose j-th column is the standard basis vector of index e(j). Since 1 − I_e·I_eᵀ is the diagonal projection onto the coordinates outside e(r), this says: every column of z whose index is not in the image of e is the corresponding column of the identity matrix.

members.name: rowStabilizer
members.statement_lean: noncomputable def rowStabilizer : Subgroup (GL N R)
members.text: For commutative rings R and S, finite types r and N, a type c, a ring homomorphism φ : R → S, a c×N matrix w over S and an embedding e : r ↪ N, rowStabilizer φ w e is the subgroup of GL_N(R) whose elements are the invertible matrices A with FixesColsOff e A (the columns of A outside the image of e are those of the identity) and w·φ(A) = w, where φ(A) applies φ to each entry. Lean builds it as an intersection of a stabiliser and the preimage under GL_N(φ) of the stabiliser of w for right multiplication, with its carrier replaced by (definitionally) this set.

members.name: columnDatum_mul_ite_eq
members.statement_lean:
lemma columnDatum_mul_ite_eq {F : _ → ℂ} (hF : ∀ A ∈ rowStabilizer φ w e, ∀ y, F (A.1 * y) = F y)
  (y : Matrix N a R) z : columnDatum χ φ w e (z.submatrix id e) * ite (FixesColsOff e z) (F y) 0 =
  ite (∃ Z ∈ rowStabilizer φ w e, Z = z) (χ z.det * F (z⁻¹ * y)) 0
members.text: Let R and S be commutative rings, r and N finite types, a and c types, χ : R → ℂ a multiplicative character, φ : R → S a ring homomorphism, w a c×N matrix over S and e : r ↪ N an embedding. Let F be a complex function on the N×a matrices over R that is invariant under left multiplication by H = rowStabilizer φ w e (hF: F(A·y) = F(y) for every A ∈ H and every y). Then for every N×a matrix y over R and every N×N matrix z over R: columnDatum χ φ w e (z_e) · (F(y) if FixesColsOff e z, else 0) = χ(det z)·F(z⁻¹·y) if z is the matrix of an element of H, and 0 otherwise. Here z_e is the N×r matrix of the columns e(r) of z and z⁻¹ the inverse matrix.

members.statement_lean: def HasWeightNormLe (p : Prop) κ F b
members.text: For finite types Φ and n, a proposition p, a weight κ (for each place τ ∈ Φ a function ℕ → ℕ of column multiplicities), a polynomial F and a real number b: HasWeightNormLe p κ F b means that there is a complex coordinate vector ξ, indexed by the standard fillings of weight κ, with toPoly n κ ξ = F (that is, F = Σ_i (Gξ)_i b_i, where b_i are the basis products of minors of weight κ and G = weylGram n κ is the integer Gram matrix of the reproducing kernel), and such that if p holds then weylNormSq ξ = Re(ξ*·G·ξ) ≤ b.

lemma HasWeightNormLe.prod {p ι} {s : Finset ι} {κ F b} :
  (∀ i ∈ s, @HasWeightNormLe Φ n _ _ p (κ i) (F i) (b i)) →

members.text: Let Φ and n be finite types, p a proposition, ι a type, s a finite subset of ι, and for each i ∈ ι a weight κ i, a polynomial F i and a real number b i. If HasWeightNormLe p (κ i) (F i) (b i) holds for every i ∈ s, then HasWeightNormLe p (Σ_{i∈s} κ i) (∏_{i∈s} F i) (∏_{i∈s} b i) holds: the product of the polynomials is the polynomial of a coordinate vector of the summed weight, whose squared norm is, when p holds, at most the product of the bounds.

members.text: For types E, r and n, with E a field carrying a CM type (CMType E) and Weil data (WeilData E) and r, n finite, an auxiliary pair O : AuxPair E r n consists of: level places of E (it extends LevelPlaces E: finite index types and two families of finite places of E, the chosen places w_i, whose product is M, and the twist places q_j, whose product is Q, the joint family injective and no place conjugate to another); signs s = O.signs : r → {±1}; a hermitian space W = O.W of rank |r| with signs s (Space E r s: a matrix J over E and a point x ∈ GL_r(𝔸_E) with xᴴ·J·x equal to diag(s) at the infinite places and to 1 at the finite places); an embedding incl : r ↪ n; a numbering ord : r → ℕ; column counts colsPlus, colsMinus : InfinitePlace E → ℕ → ℕ (the weights k⁺, k⁻: the number of columns of each height at each infinite place); a character μ of U(1)(𝔸_E) trivial on U(1)(E) (AutChar E) together with a weight (an integer at each infinite place) and a tame part ψ (a character ψ_w of the residue field at each finite place w) such that μ has this weight and tame part (hasWeight: almost all ψ_w are trivial and μ(u) = ∏_v u_v^{weight(v)}·∏_w ψ_w(u mod w) for u with integral finite part); the condition ψ_w = 1 at every finite place w that is not a place of the level (tame_eq_one); and |r| < |n| (rank_lt).

members.name: AuxPair.chosenGLRep
members.statement_lean:
def chosenGLRep {W} [AddCommGroup W] [Module ℂ W] (π : Representation ℂ _ W) :
  Representation ℂ (O.ChosenGL r) (levelSpace π _ O.levelChar)
members.text: For a field E with a CM type and Weil data, finite types r and n, and an auxiliary pair O : AuxPair E r n, a complex vector space W (W an additive commutative group with a ℂ-module structure) and a complex representation π of the finite adelic unitary group G_f of I_n on W: O.chosenGLRep π is the representation of O.ChosenGL r = ∏_i GL_r(k_{w_i}) on the subspace levelSpace π _ O.levelChar of the vectors v with π(k)v = levelChar(k)·v for k ∈ O.levelGroup, in which g acts by (∏_i ψ_{w_i}(det g_i)) times π of a lift to K₀ of the family firstBlockHom O.1 O.incl g (diag(g_i, 1) at the chosen places, 1 at the twist places) (levelRep). The definition proves that this family normalises the level and preserves the character, and that the map is multiplicative.

members.name: AuxPair.tensorPoly
members.statement_lean: def tensorPoly
members.text: For a field E with a CM type and Weil data, finite types r and n, and an auxiliary pair O : AuxPair E r n, O.tensorPoly is the ℂ-linear map from complex functions on pairs (p, q) of standard fillings (rows n; p of weight k⁺ = O.colsPlus, q of weight k⁻ = O.colsMinus) to complex polynomials in the variables X(τ, i, a) (τ an infinite place, i ∈ n, a ∈ r), sending the indicator of (p, q) to letterPoly(+1, k⁺)(δ_p)·letterPoly(−1, k⁻)(δ_q). Here letterPoly(c, k)(ξ) is the polynomial toPoly ξ of weight k in which each variable (τ, i, h) is replaced by the sum of X(τ, i, a) over the a ∈ r with O.signs a = c and O.ord a = h.

members.text: For a field E with a CM type and Weil data, finite types r and n, and an auxiliary pair O : AuxPair E r n, a finite place w of E that is split (hw: w ≠ w̄) and lies outside the places of O and their conjugates (hS), and X ∈ ℂ: O.heckePolyOnForms hw hS X is the endomorphism of O.FormV obtained by restricting the Hecke polynomial operator H_w(X) = Σ_{i=0}^{|n|} (−X)^i q^{i(i−1)/2} T_{w,i} on algebraic forms (q the norm of w, T_{w,i} the Hecke operators at w); the restriction is well defined because the forms of O.FormV are spherical at w and the Hecke operators preserve the level space (proved inside the definition).

members.name: AuxPair.heckePolyOnForms_eq_smul
members.statement_lean:
lemma heckePolyOnForms_eq_smul {y p} (h : IsSphericalWith (rightRegular ..) hw p y.1.1) X :
  O.heckePolyOnForms hw hS X y = p X • y
members.text: Let E be a field with a CM type, r and n finite types, O : AuxPair E r n, w a finite place of E with w ≠ w̄ (hw) and w not a place of O nor the conjugate of one (hS). If a form y ∈ O.FormV is spherical at w with Hecke polynomial p (h: IsSphericalWith for the right regular representation, i.e. y is fixed by K₀ at w and w̄ and H_w(T)y = p(T)·y for every T ∈ ℂ), then for every X ∈ ℂ: O.heckePolyOnForms hw hS X y = p(X)·y. (One step: the restriction commutes with the inclusion of the subspace, map_heckePolyOp, and h gives the value.)

members.name: AuxPair.Lifts

members.text: For a field E with a CM type and Weil data, finite types r and n, and an auxiliary pair O : AuxPair E r n, a form y ∈ O.FormV and a function z assigning to each finite place w of E a sequence z(w) of complex numbers: O.Lifts y z means that for every finite place w of E with w ≠ w̄ that is not a place of O nor the conjugate of one, y is spherical at w (IsSphericalWith, for the right regular representation) with Hecke polynomial T ↦ trivialHecke(q_w, |n|−|r|, ν_a(w)·T) · H_{z(w)}(q_w^{|n|−|r|}·ν_a(w)/ν_b(w)·T), where trivialHecke(q, k, X) = ∏_{0≤l<k}(1 − q^l·X), H_{z(w)}(X) = heckePolyEval r w (z w) X = Σ_{i=0}^{|r|} (−X)^i q_w^{i(i−1)/2} z(w)_i, ν_a(w) = O.a.frobValue r w and ν_b(w) = O.b.frobValue n w.

members.name: map_block_eq_blockGL
members.statement_lean:
lemma map_block_eq_blockGL {R} [CommRing R] f ε (k : Kf E N) (l : Kf E m) : ∃ h, Kf.map (S := R) n f
  ⟨U.block ε (k, l), h⟩ = reindexGL ε (blockGL (Kf.map N f k, Kf.map m f l))
members.text: Let E be a CM number field, n, N and m finite types, R a commutative ring, f : Ô_E → R a ring homomorphism from the integral finite adeles, ε : N ⊕ m ≃ n a bijection, and k ∈ K₀(N), l ∈ K₀(m) (K₀ the stabiliser of the standard lattice in the finite adelic unitary group of I_N, I_m). Then the block-diagonal element U.block ε (k, l) of the unitary group of I_n lies in K₀(n) (the witness h), and its image under Kf.map n f in GL_n(R) equals the relabelling along ε (reindexGL) of the block-diagonal matrix diag(Kf.map N f k, Kf.map m f l) (blockGL).

members.text: Let E be a field with a CM type, r, n, N, m finite types, a a type, O : AuxPair E r n, z : r ↪ m and V a divided splitting (DividedSplitting N m a O z); let k and c be types, S a k×c matrix over R₁ = O_E/M²Q (the residue ring of O.levelModulus 2) and u : c → k. members.name: Data.depth_indicator_jet
members.statement_lean:
lemma Data.depth_indicator_jet {P} (D : Data P) (m : _ → ℕ) (hm : ∀ σ, D.nominalWeight σ ≤ m σ ∧
  m σ ≤ D.nominalWeight σ + D.x ^ 42) : ∃ t ≠ 0, (∀ σ : ℂ ≃+* ℂ, ‖σ t‖ ≤ exp (D.f * D.m / D.k *
  D.b)) ∧ ∀ 𝔪, 𝔪.ideal = .span {D.piGBar} → ∀ p [Fact p.Prime] [PadicPlace p], ∃ α x₀,
  (∀ σ, ∑ i, α (σ, i, ()) = m σ) ∧ p ^ (-D.forcedPart p) ≤ ‖ιₚ (P.vacuumScale D.s ^ 12 / t * (∏ σ,
  (m σ)!) * coeff α (Space.jetSeries _ (conj ↑D.piG * P.jetScale D.s)
  (modDatum (stdSpace _ _) (stdSpace _ (Fin 12)) 𝔪 (Pi.single x₀ 1) vacVector)))‖
members.text: Let P be parameters, D admissible data over P and m a function from the infinite places σ of the field of D to ℕ with w(σ) ≤ m(σ) ≤ w(σ) + x^42 for every σ (hm; w = D.nominalWeight, x = D.x). Then there is a number t ≠ 0 with |σ(t)| ≤ exp(f·m·b/k) for every automorphism σ of ℂ (f = D.f, m = D.m, b = D.b, k = D.k: the data's), such that for every modulus 𝔪 whose ideal is generated by ϖ̄ = D.piGBar and every prime p with a chosen embedding ι_p : ℂ → ℂ_p (PadicPlace p), there are an exponent α (finitely supported on triples (σ, i, ())) and a matrix x₀ modulo 𝔪 with Σ_i α(σ, i, ()) = m(σ) for every σ and p^{−F(p)} ≤ |ι_p(κ₀^{12}/t·∏_σ m(σ)!·a)|, where a is the coefficient at α of the scaled Taylor series T_{c}(datum) (Space.jetSeries with scale c = conj(π_g)·per, π_g = D.piG, per = P.jetScale D.s) of the indicator datum: the function equal to 1 at x₀ and 0 elsewhere on matrices modulo 𝔪, tensored with the vacuum, on Hom(I_1, I_12) (modDatum). Here F = D.forcedPart and κ₀ = P.vacuumScale D.s.

lemma firstMinimum_mul_le_hom {N} [NeZero N] (hd : ↑N ∈ differentIdeal ℤ (𝓞 E)) :

members.text: Let E be a field with a CM type, n and n' finite nonempty types, s and s' signs, S a space of rank |n| with signs s and T one of rank |n'| with signs s', and N ≠ 0 a natural number in the different of E (hd).   D.Pair
members.text: For parameters P, admissible data D and a lift index j: linePair j is the function from Option {±1} to pairs (D.Pair: a character ν, coordinates c with ν of weight −c, and a point z): at none, ν = μ_j⁰·υ^{n_j} with coordinates c(σ) = w_j(σ) − n_j and z = heckeCount, n_j = j + ⌊(t − 11m − 1)/2⌋, so that ν has weight σ ↦ n_j − w_j(σ); at a sign s, ν = υ^{−e_s}·χ^{s·j} with constant coordinates c = e_s and z = e_s (e_s = eSign s: e₊ = m, e₋ = ⌊m/2⌋), so that ν has weight −e_s. The coordinates are the negatives of the characters' weights (Data.Pair imposes weight −c), which matters for the inverse characters in heckeValueProd. The definition checks the conditions of a pair. Applied to an element of Option {±1} it gives that pair.

members.statement_lean:
lemma norm_det_compressedGramOp_padic_le (ι : PrimePadicIso) (int : ∀ ζ (φ : PadicPlace ι.1),
  (∀ a, weylGauge (ι := ⟨φ.ιₚ.comp conj⟩) _ 0
  a.2.out (star (ζ a)) ≤ 1) → gl ζ ∈ integralForms φ) (h : DenominatorLe ι.2 _ D.e₀ L β) :
  ‖ι.2 (compressedGramOp (smallHookNumber j) L gl).det‖ ≤ exp (finrank ℂ L * (D.r * β))
members.text: Let P be parameters, D admissible data, j a lift index, ϑ a twist, gl a ℂ-linear map from tables (Tables j) to forms on V_j ((D.auxPair ϑ j).FormV), L a subspace of the forms on V_j and β ∈ ℝ, such that gl* is injective on L (sep) and gl(gl*(z)) is tested for every z ∈ L (tst: AuxPair.IsTested e₀ L^⊥ — orthogonal to every form of L^⊥ that is good and killed by the Hecke polynomial at the test value of some split place off the level). Let ι be a prime ℓ with an isomorphism ℂ ≅ ℚ̄_ℓ (PrimePadicIso), suppose that gl ζ is integral at every ℓ-adic place φ (LevelForm.integralForms φ) whenever conj ζ(a) is integral at its class representative for φ ∘ conj for every index a (int), and that L has denominators at most β at ι (h: DenominatorLe ι.2 _ e₀ L β). Then |ι(det(compressedGramOp 𝗁 L gl))| ≤ exp(dim L·r·β), 𝗁 = smallHookNumber j, r = D.r.

imports.name: Data
imports.lean:
structure Data (P : Parameters) where
  /-- `logX = log x`, `logB = log b`, `logX₁ = log x₁`: the sizes are chosen on the logarithmic
  scale. -/
  (logX logB logX₁ : ℝ) (s m r : ℕ) s_le : s ≤ 32 * logX
  thick : Finset _
  g : Fin 2 → ℕ
  piG : 𝓞 P.K
  scale : 1e12 * P.c ≤ log logB ∧ 100 * log logB ≤ logX ∧ 1e6 * logX ≤ logX₁ ∧ 1e6 * logX₁ ≤ logB ∧
    6 * log logX₁ ≤ log logB
  m_mem : ↑m ∈ Icc (exp (logX / 2)) (2 * exp (logX / 2))
  r_mem : ↑r ∈ Icc (exp (5 * logX)) (3 * exp (5 * logX))
  m_pow : ∃ e, m = 2 ^ (e + 1) ∧ s = (e + 1) * 22
  r_pow : ∃ e, r = 3 ^ (e + 1)
  thick_eq_neg_one_mod {m} (d : m ∣ P.N₁ s) : m ∣ P.N₀ * 3 ^ (.log 3 s + 5) → ∀ σ ∈ thick, P.placeClass d σ = -1
  three_term : let φ := P.placeClass P.two_pow_dvd_N₁; ∀ i j, 0 < i → i < j → j ≤ 324 * s →
         ∀ σ ∈ thick, ∀ τ ∈ thick, ∀ ρ ∈ thick, φ (τ / σ) ^ j = φ (ρ / σ) ^ i → φ (τ / σ) = 1
  g_prime i : (g i).Prime
  g_modEq_one i : g i ≡ 1 [MOD P.N₁ s * P.d]
  dvd_g_sub_one i : P.Mω s ^ 2 ∣ g i - 1
  g_injective : g.Injective
  g_mem i : ↑(g i) ∈ Icc (exp logB ^ 10) (exp logB ^ 11)
  norm_piG : piG * star piG = g 0 * g 1
  exists_prime_window : ∀ U ∈ Icc (100 * logB) (2 ^ s), ∃ p, p.Prime ∧ p ≡ 1 [MOD P.Mω s ^ 2] ∧
    log p ∈ Icc U (U + √logB)
imports.text: Admissible data over P: scales x, x₁, b; the exponent s and the numbers m, r; thick places with a three-term condition; primes g₀ ≠ g₁ (fields g_prime: each g i is prime, and g_modEq_one: g i ≡ 1 mod N₁·d) and an integer of K of norm g₀g₁; existence of primes ≡ 1 mod M_ω² in short windows.

imports.name: IsValuationPair.hermite
imports.lean:
lemma IsValuationPair.hermite y (wt : k → ℕ := 0) : ∃ᵉ (U ∈ intGL n R) (D : Matrix k k A),
    D.BlockTriangular wt ∧ y = U.1.submatrix id ι * D ∧ U⁻¹.1.submatrix ι id * y = D :=
  let P s U := U ∈ intGL .. ∧ ∀ j ∈ s, ∀ i ∉ (filter (wt · ≤ wt j) s).map ι, (U.1 * y) i j = 0
  have ⟨U, u, e⟩ : Exists (P univ) := univ.induction_on_max_value wt (by aesop) fun a s _ _ h ↦
    (((insert a s).map ι)ᶜ.induction_on' (motive := (∃ U, P s U ∧ ∀ i ∈ ·, (U.1 * y) i a = 0))
    (by simpa) fun i _ _ _ _ ⟨U, ⟨u, h⟩, _⟩ ↦ by
  obtain ⟨_, _, ⟨_, x, _⟩, _, _, z, _⟩ := by simpa using val ((-U.1 * y) (ι a) a) ((-U.1 * y) i a)
  exists _, ⟨mul_mem (transvectionGL_mem_intGL (.symm ?x) z) (mul_mem (transvectionGL_mem_intGL
    (?x : ι a ≠ i) (add_mem R.one_mem x)) u), ?_⟩ <;> simp at h ⊢ <;> grind +splitImp
    [mem_compl, transvection_mul_apply_same, transvection_mul_apply_of_ne]).imp (by aesop)
  ⟨_, inv_mem u, _, fun _ _ _ ↦ by apply e <;> simp [*], .symm (.trans (ext fun _ _ ↦ by
    apply sum_of_injOn _ ι.2.injOn <;> aesop) (U.1.invOf_mul_cancel_left y)), rfl⟩
imports.text: Hermite form: if (A, R) satisfies IsValuationPair and ι embeds k in n, an n×k matrix y over A is U_ι·D with U ∈ GL_n(R), U_ι its columns at ι, and D = (rows ι of U⁻¹)·y block upper triangular.

literature.verdict: Walls's stabilizer-period identity is for a different dual pair; the project proves the unitary vanishing separately
literature.comparison: Let E have a CM type and Weil data, n ≃ n₁⊕n₂ finite with the specified compatible signature identification, and let Y be continuous on the standard definite unitary group, invariant on the left by rational points, with the stated K_f level above T and its conjugate. Assume the project's DescentsVanish for the split hyperbolic unitary space of rank n₁, the specified splitting character υ^|n₁|, T and Y. For every first-block h₁ the integral of Y(block(h₁,u)) over the adelic quotient of the complementary definite unitary group vanishes. Walls Prop 2.1.1 unfolds a nondegenerate Fourier coefficient for a symplectic–orthogonal pair, with matching Schwartz data, into a stabilizer period of a convolved cusp form. Rallis treats orthogonal–symplectic towers. Neither place proves this unitary statement or passes directly from orthogonality to the chosen theta kernels to pointwise vanishing of each period. The compact source identifies the unitary stabilizer of an inclusion matrix, uses compactness/continuity in the definite case, and unfolds and separates test functions to deduce the conclusion.
sources: P. Walls, The theta correspondence, periods of automorphic forms and special values of standard automorphic L-functions, §§1.1–1.2 and §2.1, Proposition 2.1.1, equation (2.1.5), pp. 5–6. The group pair is symplectic–orthogonal and the right side is the stabilizer period of a convolved cusp form. <https://arxiv.org/pdf/1501.01565#page=6>

S. Rallis, On the Howe duality conjecture, Compositio Math. 51 (1984), introduction pp. 333–335. The formulation concerns the symplectic–orthogonal theta correspondence and its towers. <https://www.numdam.org/item/CM_1984__51_3_333_0.pdf#page=2>

literature.comparison: Let E be CM, f its number of infinite places, n its finite rank, N a nonzero natural number in the different, and L the image of V.baseLattice in the Euclidean space of real dimension m=2fn via archCoords. The signs of the Hermitian form may vary. Set λ=min(1,λ₁(L)). The statement produces an E-basis inside L of length at most 6N(fn)²/λ. The columns may generate a proper sublattice. MassBasic.lean:29–64 identifies each nonzero member of the real Euclidean dual of (2/N)L with a vector of the same length in L, using the trace pairing, the finite Hermitian self-duality condition, and N in the different. Thus λ₁(((2/N)L)*)≥λ. Banaszczyk (2.1), i=m, gives λ_m((2/N)L)≤m/λ. Scaling back, L contains m real-linearly independent vectors of length at most Nm/(2λ)=Nfn/λ. They span the real Minkowski space. Their E-span is Eⁿ because an E-subspace of rank k<n has a real Minkowski span of dimension 2fk. Select n E-independent vectors. For fn≥1 this radius implies the larger stated radius, and the rank-zero case uses the empty basis. The Lean argument uses a weaker covering-radius estimate and an induction. Lagarias–Lenstra–Schnorr Theorems 2.4–2.5 give the earlier reciprocal-minima and covering-radius inequalities.

The conclusion chooses coordinates from these very forms and gives the bound for every form in the family. The familiar real or complex normed-space theorem gives a biorthogonal unit basis but does not assert this selection from a given family in these fields. Let 𝔪 = (N) with N ≠ 0 (hN) and 𝔪 having a place (h𝔪), S a space of rank |n| with signs s, c and b characters of weights γ', γ with trivial tame parts (hc, hb), u weights dominant for the order O (hd) with holMinorsPi(s, u) integrable (hi), 2|n| < |n'| (hn), e : n ↪ n', Q₀ ≠ 0 with Fock vector holomorphic of weight u (hQ), and for each class p of the principal level N a finite family Q(p, ·) whose Fock vectors span the real translates of that of Q₀ (hs). Then for every point x there are coefficients a(p, i) such that for every ψ rapidly decreasing of level N: ∫ ψ(x·(h, 1))·holMinorsPi(s, u)(h) dh = Σ_{(p,i)} a(p, i)·∫_{[S]} ψ(g)·θ^{S, I_{n'}}_{c,b}[1_{incl e}, Q(p, i)](g, p) dg. The authors label it the basis problem in the stable range; the second reader finds the Siegel basis theorem (Böcherer) and Li's stable-range pairing related but distinct, the finite unitary formula being the artifact's own (`literature`: unresolved).

literature.verdict: The classical Siegel basis theorem and the unitary stable-range pairing are located. The finite unitary reproducing formula is distinct.
literature.comparison: Böcherer's Theorem III spans the space of degree-n Siegel modular forms of scalar weight k by theta series for k divisible by four and k>2n. Li's Theorem 2.1 gives a stable-range pairing for theta lifts of cusp-representation vectors. Lean fixes two unitary groups, the second definite of rank n′>2n, a nonzero principal ideal level with nonempty support, character weights, and a nonzero holomorphic Fock vector with integrable dominant-weight coefficient. At each definite class the specified finite list of polynomials must span its real compact-group translates. For each evaluation point x there are coefficients, independent of the rapid level-N function, expressing its convolution at x as a finite sum of pairings with explicit theta kernels. The proof uses the sharp datum attached to the inclusion matrix, realConv_eq_zero_of_lift_eq_zero, and a finite linear-duality argument. Neither published statement supplies these class-by-class finite test vectors or the point-evaluation identity.
